body:
[A10] Found on the bench by [A375] for #394 acceptance 2 (PR pending; run of 2026-09-27 on image `9e9954e9`). It confirms the #117 observation that LINK_UP/LINK_DOWN stayed flat over 7 outages.

## Problem

In the bare-metal build, nothing publishes the PHY link state.
- `sw/litex/milan_soc.py:1761-1797` defines `link_status` (MAC_STATUS 0x110, REQ-MAC-03) as a software-published CSR with reset `link_up=1`. Its own comment says the MDIO autoneg result exists only in software, and that a fabric MDIO poller would be new SystemVerilog.
- The bare-metal firmware never writes it, so `MAC_STATUS[0]` stays 1 on the shipping image.
- The consumers `milan_datapath.sv` `i_link_up` and `KL_pp_shadow.sv` `link_up_i` never see a link loss. As a result:
  - The AVB_INTERFACE LINK_UP/LINK_DOWN counters (Milan v1.2 §5.4.4, Table 5.6; IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.42) cannot advance.
  - Link-dependent behaviour (for example, re-declaring and resetting gPTP/SRP state on link return) cannot key on the real link.
  - `MAC_STATUS[2:1]` speed, which feeds `o_mac_is_1g` and the lwSRP 750 Mb/s admission limit, stays a build-time value.

On the bench, all 10 switch power cycles recovered, but MAC_STATUS stayed `0x0d` and LINK_UP/LINK_DOWN stayed `1/0`.

## Decision (manager)

- Publish the link state from the bare-metal firmware: poll the PHY BMSR and the speed/duplex result over the existing bit-bang MDIO window, and write `link_status`. No new fabric MDIO master (area directive).
- The poll period must fit the one-hart service budget of #397: heartbeat ≤ 500 ms, and no duty past the smallest deadline without a tick. This is a firmware change, so the #559 capture receipt must be re-measured.
- It runs in the same firmware lane as #590 and #592, after PR #588 merges, so there is one capture re-measure.

## Acceptance

1. The firmware publishes link up/down, speed and duplex within one poll period of a PHY change. The period is derived and stated, never mirrored.
2. A host or firmware test and a simulation check show that a link-down/up sequence increments LINK_DOWN and LINK_UP exactly once each and updates MAC_STATUS. A mutant that stops the publish is killed.
3. The #397 service-budget checks and the capture receipt pass after re-measuring.
4. **Bench:** re-run #394 acceptance 2 (ten switch cycles).
   - First prove by a read-only BMSR read whether a switch power cycle actually drops the DUT PHY link. An inline capture point sits on that link and may hold it up. If it does, STOP and report; the method needs an owner decision.
   - Otherwise every cycle shows +1/+1 on LINK_DOWN/LINK_UP.
5. REGISTER_MAP.md, BAREMETAL_FIRMWARE.md and the compliance matrix row state who publishes MAC_STATUS.

title: Publish the PHY link state from the bare-metal firmware (LINK_UP/LINK_DOWN stay flat)
